nodes.label: mcp_toolkit_command_registry.gd
nodes.summary: @tool class_name MCPToolkitCommandRegistry extends RefCounted ## Central dispatch table for MCP commands. ## ## Holds every registered command — built-in and extension — keyed by method name, ## and routes incoming calls to their handlers via [method call_command]. Built-in ## modules and extensions populate it with [method add], passing a ## [MCPToolkitCommandOptions] (or [MCPToolkitExtensionOptions]) that declares the ## command's contract; the per-command metadata it derives drives version gating, ## annotations, timeout clamping, path guards, and the read-only/serialization ## routing the dispatcher reads back through the various accessor methods here. It ## also exposes thin facades ([method create_options], [method fail], ## [method require], [method create_undo_action], [method queue_save], …) so a ## handler — including a C# one that cannot reach the GDScript statics directly — can ## build options, errors, and undo actions through this one object.[br] ## [br] ## An extension registers its commands by overriding ## [method MCPToolkitExtension.register], which receives the live registry: ## [codeblock] ## func register(registry, server): ## registry.add("physics_list_bodies", _on_list_bodies, ## MCPToolkitExtensionOptions.new("List all physics bodies").mark_read_only()) ## [/codeblock] const Modules := preload("res://addons/godot_mcp_toolkit/core/modules.gd") const Audit = Modules.Audit const FileGuard = Modules.FileGuard const _DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS := 30000 const _MIN_TIMEOUT_MS := 1000 const _MAX_TIMEOUT_MS := 300000 var _commands: Dictionary = {} var _extension_methods: Array[String] = [] var _version_blocked: Dictionary = {} # method -> {min, max, engine} # Extension-load collision guard. While an extension's register() runs (bracketed # by the loader with begin/end_extension_load), any add() of a name that is ALREADY # registered is REFUSED — recorded here, never written to _commands. This closes the # accidental-reuse footgun at load time

La caverna inicial queda en el ## origen y la final (la más lejana) guarda el altar. ## - Forma de cada caverna: unión de varias elipses con borde deformado por ruido ## (nunca un cuadrado), de 28–44 m de ancho. ## - Suelo de tierra y paredes de roca irregulares (MultiMesh, 1 llamada cada uno); ## colisión de paredes con cajas fusionadas por filas. ## - Temas por caverna: campamento (chozas, tiendas, fogata), almacén (barriles y ## cajas destruibles, empalizadas) o santuario (tótem y postes de calaveras). ## - Barriles y cajas son DestructibleProp: se rompen a golpes. ## Reutiliza de ProceduralMap el sistema de props/luces y expone get_height_at() ## (suelo plano = 0) y get_colliders() (paredes incluidas) para EnemyMotion. const CELL := 2.0 ## lado de una celda (m) const SLOT := 26 ## separación entre centros de caverna (celdas) const WALL_H := 4.0 const TUNNEL_R := 1.6 ## radio de los túneles (celdas) const DIRS := [Vector2i(1, 0), Vector2i(-1, 0), Vector2i(0, 1), Vector2i(0, -1)] const DIRS8 := [Vector2i(1, 0), Vector2i(-1, 0), Vector2i(0, 1), Vector2i(0, -1), Vector2i(1, 1), Vector2i(1, -1), Vector2i(-1, 1), Vector2i(-1, -1)] const FLOOR := 1 const CORRIDOR := 2 ## Formas de caverna (las normales eligen una al azar): ## blobs elipse principal con 2-4 lóbulos (la clásica) ## cross dos elipses alargadas cruzadas: cuatro brazos ## hall sala larga con dos filas de columnas de roca ## twin dos cámaras unidas por un cuello estrecho ## pillars la clásica con 3-5 columnas de roca para cubrirse const SHAPES := ["blobs", "cross", "hall", "twin", "pillars"] const PILLAR_R := 1.3 ## radio de las columnas (celdas) const CENTER

nodes.summary: ﻿extends Node class_name WaveManager ## Aparición CONTINUA de enemigos: no hay oleadas ni pisos. Los enemigos salen siempre y la ## presión sube con el tiempo de partida (GameState.elapsed_time): intervalo menor, lotes más ## grandes, más enemigos vivos a la vez, tipos nuevos y más vida/daño. A los BOSS_TIME_S ## aparece el Nigromante (una sola vez) y la aparición normal baja mientras siga vivo. ## Al morir el jefe se emite boss_died y se detiene la aparición. signal enemy_died(pos: Vector3, gold_val: int) signal boss_died(pos: Vector3, gold_val: int) ## 6 min + 70 s = 7:10 const BOSS_TIME_S: float = 430.0 ## Fracción de la aparición normal que se mantiene mientras el jefe está vivo. const BOSS_SPAWN_FACTOR: float = 0.35 # Curva de intensidad: se interpola de "inicio" a "final" entre 0 y BOSS_TIME_S. const INTERVAL_START: float = 1.4 const INTERVAL_END: float = 0.25 const BATCH_START: int = 1 const BATCH_END: int = 6 const ALIVE_CAP_START: int = 40 ## Escalado por minuto de partida. const HP_PER_MINUTE: float = 0.15 const DAMAGE_PER_MINUTE: float = 0.06 const PLAYABLE_MIN_X: float = -95.0 const PLAYABLE_MAX_X: float = 95.0 const PLAYABLE_MIN_Z: float = -95.0 const PLAYABLE_MAX_Z: float = 95.0 var spawn_timer: Timer var player: Node3D var wave_config: Dictionary = {} var _running: bool = false ## Apariciones pendientes: se instancian como máximo MAX_SPAWNS_PER_FRAME por frame para repartir el coste. const MAX_SPAWNS_PER_FRAME := 2 var _pending_spawns: int = 0 var _boss: Node = null var _boss_spawned: bool = false func _ready() -> void: spawn_timer = Timer.new() spawn_timer.one_shot = true add_child(spawn_timer) spawn_timer.timeout.connect(_on_spawn_tick) var manager := EnemyManager.new() # IA y pool de los enemigos normales (datos) manager.name = "EnemyManager" add_child(manager) var visuals := EnemyVisuals.new() # los dibuja con MultiMesh visuals.name = "EnemyVisuals" add_child(visuals) _load_wave_config() func _load_wave_config() -> void:

nodes.summary: class_name SpiritHippo extends SpiritAnimal ## Cabeza de hipopótamo espiritual (melee): emerge del suelo sobre el grupo de enemigos más ## denso y los devora. Su "estómago" tiene capacidad según el tamaño de cada enemigo ## (pequeño = 1, mediano = 2, grande = 3). Lo que no cabe recibe un mordisco normal. const MODEL = preload("res://assets/models/spirits/hippo.glb") const BASE_CAPACITY := 3 const MOUTH_RADIUS := 2.3 const MOUTH_FORWARD := 0.9 ## m (a escala 1) del origen de la cabeza al centro de la boca const RISE_TIME := 0.3 const RISE_DEPTH := 1.6 const NO_FIT := 99 ## coste de lo que no se puede devorar (jefes) var capacity: int = BASE_CAPACITY var center: Vector3 = Vector3.ZERO var facing: Vector3 = Vector3.FORWARD var eaten: int = 0 var eaten_cost: int = 0 var bitten: int = 0 ## enemigos que no cupieron y solo recibieron daño var _ground: Vector3 ## Cuánto "estómago" ocupa un enemigo. static func devour_cost(e) -> int: if "type" in e and "max_hp" in e and e.max_hp <= 400.0: match int(e.type): 2: return 3 # HEAVY_BRUTE 4: return 2 # ZOMBIE_GOBLIN _: return 1 return NO_FIT ## El enemigo con más vecinos dentro del radio de la boca (empate: el más cercano al jugador). static func pick_target(tree: SceneTree, from: Vector3, search_range: float): var cands: Array = [] for e in EnemyRegistry.all(): if is_instance_valid(e) and e.global_position.distance_to(from) <= search_range: cands.append(e) var best = null var best_n := -1 var best_d := INF for e in cands: var n := 0 for o in cands: var off: Vector3 = o.global_position - e.global_position off.y = 0.0 if off.length() <= MOUTH_RADIUS: n += 1 var d: float = e.global_position.distance_to(from) if n > best_n or (n == best_n and d < best_d): best = e best_n = n best_d = d return best static func summon(parent: Node, p: Node3D, enemy, dmg: float, size: float, weapon: int, cap: int = BASE_CAPACITY) -> SpiritHippo: var

nodes.summary: class_name SpiritKomodo extends SpiritAnimal ## Dragón de Komodo espiritual (melee): se invoca delante del jugador mirando HACIA ATRÁS ## y ataca con la cola, que acaba sobre los enemigos dejándolos sangrando. Cada invocación ## hace una de tres animaciones (sin repetir la anterior): ## Es el "Stand" de Joel (estilo JoJo): brota diminuto de su espalda, sube por encima de su cabeza ## creciendo, se lanza en picado hacia delante girando hasta quedar con la cola hacia el enemigo y ## ataca; al terminar vuelve a meterse en la espalda de Joel encogiéndose (StandAura pone el aura ## y los ゴゴゴ): ## latigazo — se enrosca y chasquea la cola de lado a lado. ## torbellino — salta y gira tres vueltas con la cola extendida (3 golpes, 360°). ## martillazo — se alza, arquea la cola sobre sí mismo y la estrella contra el suelo. ## Solo en la mazmorra: en supervivencia sigue la animación y el golpe de siempre (LEGACY). const MODEL = preload("res://assets/models/spirits/komodo.glb") const TAIL_ROOT := 0.9 ## m desde el centro del komodo hasta el inicio de la cola const TAIL_LENGTH := 3.4 ## m de cola const BLEED_DPS_FACTOR := 0.35 ## dps de sangrado = daño del golpe × factor const BLEED_TIME := 4.0 ## fan: semiángulo del abanico (≥180 = círculo completo) · dmg: × daño del espíritu por golpe · ## kb: empuje (m/s) · strikes: segundos (desde que empieza la animación) de cada golpe · ## shake: temblor de cámara en el golpe · land: s hasta que aterriza (polvo y temblor). const VARIANTS := [ {"anim": "latigazo", "strikes": [0.71], "fan": 80.0, "reach": 1.0, "dmg": 1.0, "kb": 13.0, "shake": 0.3, "land": 0.42, "whoosh": 0.9}, {"anim": "torbellino", "strikes": [0.75, 1.17, 1.59], "fan": 180.0, "reach": 0.95, "dmg": 0.6, "kb": 9.0, "shake": 0.22, "land": 0.42, "whoosh": 1.2}, {"anim": "martillazo", "strikes": [0.75], "fan": 55.0, "reach": 1.15, "dmg": 1.5, "kb": 20.0, "shake": 0.65, "land": 0.42, "whoosh": 0.6, "slam": true}, ] ## Supervivencia: exactamente

nodes.summary: class_name SpiritOwl extends SpiritAnimal ## Búho espiritual (a distancia): vuela desde arriba, se lanza en picada sobre el enemigo, ## lo golpea (daño en un radio pequeño + veneno) y se aleja ascendiendo. const MODEL = preload("res://assets/models/spirits/owl.glb") const HIT_RADIUS := 1.9 const POISON_DPS_FACTOR := 0.3 const POISON_TIME := 5.0 const KNOCKBACK := 7.0 const START_HEIGHT := 3.2 const EXIT_TIME := 0.7 var target = null var hits: int = 0 var _start: Vector3 var _target_pos: Vector3 var _strike_pos: Vector3 var _exit_pos: Vector3 var _dir: Vector3 = Vector3.FORWARD var _prev_pos: Vector3 ## Invoca un búho que atacará a `enemy`. static func summon(parent: Node, p: Node3D, enemy, dmg: float, size: float, weapon: int) -> SpiritOwl: var o := SpiritOwl.new() o.player = p o.target = enemy o.damage = dmg o.scale_mult = size o.source_weapon = weapon o.strike_time = 0.55 parent.add_child(o) var d: Vector3 = enemy.global_position - p.global_position d.y = 0.0 o._dir = d.normalized() if d.length_squared() > 0.0001 else Vector3.FORWARD o._start = p.global_position + Vector3(0, START_HEIGHT * size, 0) - o._dir * 1.5 o._target_pos = enemy.global_position + Vector3(0, 0.9, 0) o.global_position = o._start o._prev_pos = o._start o.build(MODEL) o._face(o._target_pos - o._start) return o func _face(v: Vector3) -> void: if v.length_squared() > 0.0001: look_at(global_position + v.normalized(), Vector3.UP) func _motion(_delta: float) -> void: if not struck: if is_instance_valid(target): _target_pos = target.global_position + Vector3(0, 0.9, 0) var s := clampf(_elapsed / strike_time, 0.0, 1.0) s = s * s * (3.0 - 2.0 * s) * 0.6 + s * 0.4 # arranque suave, picada decidida global_position = _start.lerp(_target_pos, s) else: var s2 := clampf((_elapsed - strike_time) / EXIT_TIME, 0.0, 1.5) global_position = _strike_pos.lerp(_exit_pos, s2 * s2 * 0.5 + s2 * 0.5) var v := global_position - _prev_pos if v.length_squared() > 0.00001:

nodes.summary: class_name PlayerStatBlock extends Node ## Resuelve las estadísticas "de partida" del jugador a partir de los objetos ## recogidos (InventoryComponent) y del modo Tryhard. Es la ÚNICA fuente de ## verdad: movimiento, combate, supervivencia y economía le preguntan a este ## nodo en lugar de leer ItemDB por su cuenta. ## ## Convenciones de ItemDB (claves de "stats"): ## move_speed +fracción de velocidad (0.12 = +12 %) ## jump_height +fracción de altura de salto ## extra_jumps +saltos aéreos extra (entero) ## attack_speed +fracción de velocidad de ataque (cooldown = 1 / (1 + x)) ## cooldown_reduction fracción de cooldown eliminada ## extra_projectiles +proyectiles extra por disparo (armas "ranged") ## melee_hits +golpes extra por ataque (armas "melee") ## melee_size +fracción de tamaño de ataques melee ## ranged_size +fracción de tamaño de proyectiles ## damage +fracción de daño ## armor fracción de daño recibido que se anula (tope 85 %) ## max_hp +vida máxima (se aplica una sola vez al recoger) ## hp_regen +vida por segundo ## magnet +metros de radio de atracción de XP ## gold +fracción de oro obtenido ## tryhard nivel de Tryhard (0 = apagado) signal stats_recalculated const TRYHARD_SPEED := 0.25 const TRYHARD_DAMAGE := 0.40 const TRYHARD_ARMOR := 0.20 const TRYHARD_SPAWN_RATE := 1.5 ## más enemigos por oleada const TRYHARD_SPAWN_INTERVAL := 0.65 ## intervalo de spawn multiplicado const CAP_MOVE := 1.0 ## +100 % de velocidad como máximo const CAP_JUMP := 0.8 const CAP_EXTRA_JUMPS := 3 const CAP_EXTRA_PROJECTILES := 5 const CAP_MELEE_HITS := 3 const CAP_SIZE := 1.0 const CAP_ARMOR := 0.85 const MIN_COOLDOWN_MULT := 0.3 const CAP_TRYHARD := 1 var _player: Node var _inventory: InventoryComponent var _applied_regen: float = -1.0 func _ready() -> void: _player = get_parent() _inventory = _p

nodes.summary: class_name StatusEffects extends Node ## Estados alterados (veneno, sangrado, quemadura) para enemigos y jugador. ## Se crea bajo demanda con StatusEffects.apply_to(host, ...); el host solo necesita ## take_damage(amount). Cada tick llama a take_damage en modo "daño continuo" (los ## enemigos agrupan números/destellos/sonido) y avisa a on_damage_dealt (robo de vida). ## ## veneno : acumula hasta 5 cargas; cada carga hace su dps. ## sangrado : hasta 3 cargas; +50 % de daño mientras el objetivo se mueve. ## quemadura: no acumula (gana el dps mayor); daño alto y corto. signal effect_changed(effect_id: String) const TICK := 0.5 const MOVING_SPEED := 0.6 const EFFECTS := { "poison": {"name": "Veneno", "icon": "☠", "color": Color(0.45, 1.0, 0.3), "max_stacks": 5, "stacks": true}, "bleed": {"name": "Sangrado", "icon": "🩸", "color": Color(0.95, 0.12, 0.12), "max_stacks": 3, "stacks": true}, "burn": {"name": "Quemadura", "icon": "🔥", "color": Color(1.0, 0.52, 0.12), "max_stacks": 1, "stacks": false}, } var host = null # Node (jugador) o EnemyData ## id -> {dps, time_left, stacks, source, weapon} var active: Dictionary = {} var _tick_acc: float = 0.0 var _vfx: Dictionary = {} static var _soft_tex: GradientTexture2D = null static var _quad: QuadMesh = null static var _mats: Dictionary = {} ## Aplica (o refresca) un estado sobre cualquier nodo con take_damage(). ## source = jugador que lo causó (robo de vida); source_weapon = tipo de arma o -1. static func apply_to(target, effect_id: String, dps: float, duration: float, source: Node = null, source_weapon: int = -1, add_stacks: int = 1) -> void: if target == null or not is_instance_valid(target) or not EFFECTS.has(effect_id): return var comp := get_for(target) if comp == null: comp = StatusEffects.new() comp.name = "StatusEffects" comp.host = target if target is Node: target.add_child(comp) else: # Enemigo de datos: el componente vive bajo el EnemyManager y guarda su referencia en el en

nodes.summary: class_name Quality extends RefCounted ## Nivel de calidad gráfica (Bajo / Medio / Alto). Android arranca en Medio y PC en Alto; el valor ## guardado por el jugador (SettingsManager.quality_level) tiene prioridad. Todo lo que cuesta ## rendimiento (partículas, luces dinámicas, sombras, resolución 3D, tope de enemigos) consulta aquí. enum Level { LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH } static var _level: int = -1 ## Para probar el modo móvil en PC: lanzar con la variable de entorno RUMBANG_FORCE_MOBILE=1. ## Móvil: Android/iOS nativos y también el navegador de un móvil (versión web en iPhone o Android). static func is_mobile() -> bool: return OS.get_name() in ["Android", "iOS"] or OS.has_feature("web_ios") or OS.has_feature("web_android") or OS.get_environment("RUMBANG_FORCE_MOBILE") == "1" ## SettingsManager es un autoload: se busca en el árbol (no por identificador) para que este script ## compile también cuando se carga fuera del juego (importación, pruebas). static func _settings() -> Node: var tree := Engine.get_main_loop() as SceneTree return tree.root.get_node_or_null("SettingsManager") if tree else null static func level() -> int: if _level < 0: var st := _settings() var saved: int = int(st.get("quality_level")) if st else -1 if saved >= 0 and saved <= Level.HIGH: _level = saved else: _level = Level.MEDIUM if is_mobile() else Level.HIGH _apply_vfx() return _level static func set_level(l: int) -> void: _level = clampi(l, Level.LOW, Level.HIGH) _apply_vfx() var st := _settings() if st: st.set("quality_level", _level) st.call("save_settings") ## Enemigos como impostores (sprites con varios ángulos): por defecto en móvil. Se puede forzar con la ## variable de entorno RUMBANG_IMPOSTORS=1 (activar) o 0 (desactivar). static func use_impostors() -> bool: var env := OS.get_environment("RUMBANG_IMPOSTORS") if env == "1": return true if env == "0": return false return is_mobile() ## Pasa el nivel a los shaders de efectos (uniforme global vfx_q

nodes.label: unfocused_backup.gd
nodes.summary: @tool extends RefCounted ## Machine-wide, version-keyed, first-writer-wins backup of the TRUE original ## value of the global EditorSetting ## `interface/editor/unfocused_low_processor_mode_sleep_usec`. ## ## The toolkit lowers that key to keep the editor responsive while it is ## unfocused and an MCP client is connected, then restores it on the last ## disconnect. Because the live restore is in-memory, a crash (after a settings ## `save()` flushed the boost to disk) or a concurrent second editor could ## otherwise strand the global key at the boosted value — and, worse, re-read ## that boosted value as the "original" on the next launch, losing the true ## default forever (the same root bug for both the crash and the concurrent ## case: reading a boosted value as the original). ## ## This helper persists `{original, boosted}` to a sibling file in the ## machine-wide registry dir so the true original survives both a crash and a ## concurrent instance. The decision logic (`resolve_restore`, ## `should_capture_boost`) is pure and headless-unit-testable; file I/O takes an ## explicit `dir` so tests use a temp dir. Cross-instance atomicity ## (first-writer-wins) is provided by the CALLER holding the registry file lock ## around `capture_if_absent` / `delete_backup` (see mcp_server.gd) — this script ## does no locking itself, keeping it pure. ## ## File name: `unfocused_sleep_backup_<major.minor>.json` — version-keyed so two ## Godot editor versions running at once never conflate their separate ## EditorSettings. const _FILENAME_PREFIX := "unfocused_sleep_backup_" ## "<major>.<minor>" for the running engine, used to key the backup file. ## Pass a `{major, minor}` dict to override (unit tests). static func version_key(version_info: Dictionary = {}) -> String: var vi := version_info if not version_info.is_empty() else Engine.get_version_info() return "%d.%d" % [int(vi.get("major", 0)), int(vi.get("minor", 0))] static func backup_path(dir: String, ver: String) -> Stri

nodes.label: unfocused_sleep_controller.gd
nodes.summary: @tool extends RefCounted ## Lowers / restores the machine-wide unfocused-sleep EditorSetting while an MCP ## client is connected, crash-safe via the first-writer-wins backup. ## ## When the editor loses focus, Godot's unfocused_low_processor_mode_sleep_usec ## (default ~100000 µs ≈ 10 fps) throttles _process. Since the server polls the ## WebSocket in _process, that slows MCP interactions to ~2-3 Hz — and the editor ## is normally UNFOCUSED during an MCP session (the user is on the chat), so this ## is the common case, not an edge. While an authenticated client is connected AND ## the user has opted in, this lowers the sleep to keep the editor responsive ## unfocused, then restores it on the last disconnect / stop. ## ## The key is a machine-wide EditorSetting (every project on this editor version), ## and set_setting only reaches disk on a later save() — so a crash (after a flush) ## or a concurrent second editor could strand it at the boosted value and, worse, ## re-read that as the "original" on the next launch, losing the true default. We ## guard against that with a machine-wide, version-keyed, first-writer-wins backup ## of the TRUE original (in the registry dir, under the registry lock) plus a ## conflict-aware restore and a startup self-heal. Opt-in + tunable rate live in ## EditorSettings (registered in plugin.gd::_register_editor_settings). ## ## Editor-side ONLY — and TAINTED by design: it drives EditorSettings (via the ## injected accessor) and the registry lock. That is allowed because the Mode-B ## runtime autoload has NO unfocused sleep and must NEVER preload this file. #91713 ## therefore does not gate this child, but a runtime reference to it WOULD taint the ## autoload, so keep it strictly editor-only: only mcp_server.gd (the editor server) ## preloads it. The orchestrator owns the cross-subsystem TRIGGER points (first ## authed connect → lower; last disconnect → restore; start() → self-heal first); ## this child owns only the MECHANISM behind each

nodes.label: log_buffer.gd
nodes.summary: @tool extends RefCounted ## In-memory ring buffer capturing ALL console output. ## ## Two capture strategies, selected automatically at setup(): ## ## Godot 4.5+ — Logger subclass (compiled at runtime via GDScript.new() ## to avoid parse errors on older versions). Captures ## print(), printerr(), push_warning(), push_error(), ## engine errors, shader errors. Zero latency. ## ## Godot 4.2–4.4 — Log file tailing. poll() reads new bytes from the ## configured log path since the last read offset. ## ~500ms polling interval, subject to Godot's ## file-flush timing. ## ## Thread safety: Logger callbacks can fire from any thread. ## All buffer access is Mutex-protected. const LogHelpers := preload("res://addons/godot_mcp_toolkit/logging/log_helpers.gd") # Export-clean (core APIs only) — safe in the runtime autoload's preload closure, # which pulls this file in. const VersionUtils := preload("res://addons/godot_mcp_toolkit/versioning/mcp_version_utils.gd") const _CAPACITY := 500 const _POLL_INTERVAL_MS := 200 const _SCRIPT_ERROR_LATCH_CAPACITY := 16 # -- Shared state (Mutex-protected) ------------------------------------------ static var _mutex: Mutex = Mutex.new() static var _entries: Array = [] static var _next_id: int = 0 # Structured {id, file, line} locations of captured SCRIPT errors (Logger # error_type 2), latched beside their console entries. A separate side-channel # on purpose: console entries keep their {id, timestamp_unix, level, message} # wire shape, while script_check recovers the real parse line of a reload it # just ran. Only the 4.5+ Logger fills it — the 4.2-4.4 file tail has no # structured line data. static var _script_error_locations: Array = [] # -- Strategy tracking -------------------------------------------------------- static var _use_logger: bool = false static var _setup_done: bool = false static var _logger_ref = null # prevent GC — OS.add_logg

nodes.label: scene_lease.gd
nodes.summary: @tool extends RefCounted ## Coordinates the time-bounded per-scene editing lease + the scene-affinity queue ## that keep concurrent peers targeting different scenes from contaminating each ## other's edited tab. It owns the lease state (holder / scene / renewal stamp), the ## per-peer scene affinity, and the FIFO of tab-dependent commands waiting on the ## lease — plus the full mechanism over them: acquire / renew / release / steal ## (TTL expiry) / drain, scene.open contention handling, and the queued-command ## execution path. The dispatch layer ROUTES into this child's public API; the ## routing itself lives in the scene-lease lane (dispatch_lane.gd), not here. ## ## Editor-side ONLY — and TAINTED by design: it names EditorInterface (via the ## injected root-resolver) and reaches Modules.CommandHelpers.open_scene_deferred. That is ## allowed because the Mode-B runtime autoload has NO scene lease and must NEVER ## preload this file (it has no affinity/tab concept — a running game always owns ## its single SceneTree). #91713 therefore does not gate this child, but a runtime ## reference to it WOULD taint the autoload, so keep it strictly editor-only: only ## mcp_server.gd (the editor server) preloads it. ## ## Seams the dispatcher / mutation lane inject (so this child does not reach back ## into not-yet-extracted server internals, mirroring mutation_watchdog's ## force_clear hook): a root-resolver Callable (the testability seam — the editor ## injects EditorInterface.get_edited_scene_root, a unit test injects a stub), the ## command_received re-emit, the read-only execute core, the mutation busy-enqueue, ## and the mutation-lane entry. The registry is held directly (set_registry), like ## the server holds it, because the drain + scene.open paths query it and call ## commands. Notifier / FileGuard / MCPToolkitError / open_scene_deferred are ## reached directly (this child is tainted, so the clean-closure rule does not bind ## it) exactly as the server's _send_* wrap

nodes.summary: @tool class_name MCPToolkitCommandOptions extends RefCounted ## Fluent builder for the options a command declares when registered. ## ## Every chainable method returns [code]self[/code], so a registration reads as a ## single chain whose terminal [method to_dict] produces the metadata dictionary ## [method MCPToolkitCommandRegistry.add] consumes. Each setter records one facet ## of the command's contract: its hints ([method mark_read_only], ## [method mark_destructive], [method mark_idempotent]), its dispatch behaviour ## ([method mark_exclusive_execution], [method mark_scene_independent], ## [method with_timeout_ms]), its grouping ([method with_group]), its version range ## ([method with_min_godot_version] / [method with_max_godot_version]), and its ## path guards ([method guard_project_path] / [method guard_user_path]).[br] ## [br] ## For built-in tools, only [method mark_read_only] is load-bearing ## (routing/serialization); the client-visible readOnly/destructive/idempotent hints ## are server-authoritative (server [code]src/catalogue.ts[/code]). ## [method mark_destructive] / [method mark_idempotent] apply only to EXTENSION ## tools, whose annotations the bridge reads via ## [method MCPToolkitCommandRegistry.get_command_metadata]. Extension tools should ## use [MCPToolkitExtensionOptions], a subclass that requires a description at ## construction time (it errors on an empty one but still constructs).[br] ## [br] ## Example — register a read-only physics tool: ## [codeblock] ## registry.add("physics_list_bodies", _on_list_bodies, ## MCPToolkitCommandOptions.new() \ ## .mark_read_only() \ ## .with_timeout_ms(60000) \ ## .with_group("physics_tools", "Physics inspection", ["physics", "force"])) ## [/codeblock] var _description: String = "" var _input_schema: Dictionary = {} var _is_read_only: bool = false var _is_destructive: bool = false var _is_idempotent: bool = false var _is_cancellable: bool = false var _timeout_ms: int = 0 # 0 =

nodes.summary: @tool extends RefCounted ## Repository for the project-root .mcp.json file. ## ## Owns all plugin access to .mcp.json: it reads (path resolution, the ## godot-mcp-toolkit server entry's env vars, read-only detection) AND builds ## the plugin-initiated write. The write is OS-aware — it emits a per-OS ## mcpServers command/args (bare npx on macOS/Linux, cmd /c npx on Windows; a ## GODOT_MCP_DEV_SERVER_PATH override emits the local-dist node form). The file ## stays user-owned for edits; the plugin writes it only on explicit user action ## (the dock's / Tools-menu's "Write .mcp.json"), preserving an existing file's ## GODOT_MCP_* env keys. ## ## UI-free by design: the write reports its outcome through an injected ## on_result Callable so the overwrite-confirmation dialog stays in the ## shared write flow and the feedback (toast) stays with each caller; this ## repository touches only the file and never reaches EditorInterface / ## a dialog / a toast. # Bundled env/shape skeleton: the write reads its env block for the base env # (GODOT_MCP_CONFIG_VERSION); the per-OS builder overlays command/args. const _TEMPLATE_PATH := "res://addons/godot_mcp_toolkit/.mcp.json.template" # The mcpServers key the toolkit owns in .mcp.json. const _SERVER_KEY := "godot-mcp-toolkit" # Released npm package the client launches — the default (release) command base. const _RELEASE_PACKAGE := "@npgamedev/godot-mcp-server" # Optional env override: set to a local dist/index.js and the builder emits the # dev form ([code]node <that path>[/code]) instead of the released npx form — one # path serving Windows dogfooding and pointing a Mac at a local build. The path is # read from the environment at build time; no machine path is ever hardcoded here. const _DEV_SERVER_PATH_ENV := "GODOT_MCP_DEV_SERVER_PATH" # Reused JSON parser — avoids allocating a JSON on every poll (the dock re-checks # .mcp.json validity ~1s). nodes.label: scrubber.gd
nodes.summary: @tool extends RefCounted ## Secret scrubber — redacts credentials from log/error output before ## returning it through the MCP transport. Applied to debugger_get_log ## and editor_get_console; never applied to ## script_read (source code should not be mutated). # Three high-precision patterns that cover real secrets with minimal # false-positives. The broad hex pattern ([A-Fa-f0-9]{32,}) is # deliberately omitted — false-positives on Godot UIDs, asset hashes, # and import checksums outweigh the marginal secret-detection gain. # Add patterns here only when a concrete leak is found. const PATTERNS: Array[String] = [ "(?i)(api[_-]?key|token|secret|password)\\s*[:=]\\s*[\\w\\.\\-]+", "sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}", "(?i)bearer\\s+[A-Za-z0-9\\.\\-_]+", ] ## Compiled once at script load. static var _compiled_patterns: Array[RegEx] = _compile_patterns() static func _compile_patterns() -> Array[RegEx]: var out: Array[RegEx] = [] for pattern in PATTERNS: var regex := RegEx.new() regex.compile(pattern) out.append(regex) return out ## Scrub secrets from text. Returns {text: String, redaction_count: int}. ## When redaction_count > 0 and source is non-empty, emits a push_warning ## so developers can correlate [REDACTED] appearances with the scrubber. static func scrub(text: String, source: String = "") -> Dictionary: var out := text var redaction_count := 0 for regex in _compiled_patterns: var matches := regex.search_all(out) redaction_count += matches.size() out = regex.sub(out, "[REDACTED]", true) if redaction_count > 0 and not source.is_empty(): push_warning("[Scrubber] %d redactions applied to %s" % [redaction_count, source]) return {"text": out, "redaction_count": redaction_count}

nodes.label: untrusted.gd
nodes.summary: @tool extends RefCounted ## Untrusted-content envelope wrapper. ## ## Wraps user-authored / project-authored content in a nonce-tagged ## <untrusted-{nonce}> envelope before it is returned to the LLM. ## Scrubs existing envelope tags from the body to prevent tag-breakout ## injection. Never applied to write paths or binary (screenshot) data. ## Compiled once at script load — one allocation per editor session. static var _envelope_tag_re: RegEx = _compile_envelope_re() static func _compile_envelope_re() -> RegEx: var re := RegEx.new() re.compile("(?i)<\\s*/?\\s*untrusted(?:-[0-9a-f]*)?(?:\\s[^>]*)?>") return re static func wrap(kind: String, source: String, body: String) -> String: var nonce := "%08x" % randi() var scrubbed := _scrub_envelope_tags(body) return '<untrusted-%s kind="%s" source="%s">\n%s\n</untrusted-%s>' % [nonce, kind, source, scrubbed, nonce] static func _scrub_envelope_tags(text: String) -> String: return _envelope_tag_re.sub(text, "[scrubbed-envelope-tag]", true)

nodes.label: dungeon_goblin.gd
nodes.summary: class_name DungeonGoblin extends CharacterBody3D ## Goblin cuerpo a cuerpo del modo mazmorra (un nodo por enemigo, con animaciones reales). ## ## Estados: IDLE → APPROACH → WINDUP (telegrafía) → ATTACK (ventana de golpe) → RECOVER ## (vulnerable) y HURT / STAGGER al recibir golpes; DEAD al morir. ## Tres ataques (ATTACKS), elegidos por distancia, cada uno con su forma de evitarlo: ## - swipe (zarpazo): pegado al jugador; anticipación corta y cono ancho y corto → alejarse. ## - slam (porrazo a dos puños): media distancia; puños en alto y cuña larga → salir de la cuña. ## - leap (embestida): de lejos; se agacha y se lanza en línea recta (franja en el suelo) → ## apartarse de lado. Si choca contra una pared durante la embestida, se aturde. ## Todos son legibles y evitables: pose + destello rojo + aviso en el suelo que se rellena + ## gruñido. La orientación se fija antes de golpear y el daño solo se aplica dentro de la ## ventana del ataque, una vez, si el jugador está en la zona y sin pared en medio. ## - Comparte el contrato de EnemyData: está en EnemyRegistry (lo encuentran MeleeHitbox, ## EnemyQuery, el apuntado suave y la lanza lanzada), take_damage(amount, dir), ## apply_knockback(v), hit_radius / hit_height, y avisa a HitFeedback. ## Los valores de combate son iniciales: se ajustan jugando (Fase D de AUDITORIA_COMBATE_MAZMORRAS.md). ## ## Color del aviso según cómo se evita (como los anillos de God of War, ver guard_kind): ## ámbar = cuerpo a cuerpo, se para con un parry · rojo = área, solo se esquiva · ## azul = proyectil, la guardia reduce el daño. ## Barra de aturdimiento: se llena con golpes (más con los pesados, al castigar la recuperación ## y con los parry) y se vacía sola si se le deja en paz. Llena → STUNNED: queda indefenso unos ## segundos y se le puede rematar (PlayerFinisherController → receive_finisher). signal died(goblin: DungeonGoblin) ## STUNNED va al final: el número de cada estado viaja en las instantáneas de red (NetWorld)

Cada equipo la deja con su ## copia de la babosa (también las marionetas), así que no viaja por la red. const LIFETIME := 5.0 const FADE := 1.2 ## s finales en los que se desvanece const SLOW := 0.7 ## velocidad del jugador encima const COLOR := Color(0.45, 0.6, 0.12, 0.75) static var _mesh: Mesh var radius := 0.6 var _t := 0.0 var _mat: StandardMaterial3D static func spawn(parent: Node, at: Vector3, p_radius: float) -> SlimePuddle: var s := SlimePuddle.new() s.radius = p_radius parent.add_child(s) s.global_position = Vector3(at.x, at.y + 0.03, at.z) s.rotation.y = randf() * TAU return s func _ready() -> void: if _mesh == null: var disc := CylinderMesh.new() disc.top_radius = 1.0 disc.bottom_radius = 1.0 disc.height = 0.01 disc.radial_segments = 14 disc.rings = 1 _mesh = disc var mi := MeshInstance3D.new() mi.mesh = _mesh mi.scale = Vector3(radius * randf_range(0.85, 1.15), 1.0, radius * randf_range(0.7, 1.0)) _mat = StandardMaterial3D.new() _mat.transparency = BaseMaterial3D.TRANSPARENCY_ALPHA _mat.albedo_color = COLOR _mat.roughness = 0.1 _mat.metallic_specular = 0.9 mi.material_override = _mat mi.cast_shadow = GeometryInstance3D.SHADOW_CASTING_SETTING_OFF add_child(mi) func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void: _t += delta if _t >= LIFETIME: queue_free() return _mat.albedo_color.a = COLOR.a * clampf((LIFETIME - _t) / FADE, 0.0, 1.0) if Net.is_dedicated(): return var p := get_tree().get_first_node_in_group("player") as Node3D if p == null: return var off := p.global_position - global_position if absf(off.y) > 0.6 or Vector2(off.x, off.z).length() > radius: return var mc = p.get("movement_controller") if mc != null: var now := Time.get_ticks_msec() / 1000.0 mc

nodes.summary: class_name DungeonDoor extends Node3D ## Barrera rúnica que tapa una boca de túnel mientras hay goblins vivos en la caverna (mazmorra). ## Una columna de energía roja por celda de la boca, con colisión en la capa del mundo (frena al ## jugador y a los goblins). Sube del suelo al cerrarse y se hunde al abrirse. ## En las cloacas (WorldDefs "door": "bars") es una reja de barrotes oxidados en vez de energía. const CELL := 2.0 const HEIGHT := 3.6 const COLOR := Color(1.0, 0.18, 0.12) const BAR_COLOR := Color(0.3, 0.22, 0.16) const BAR_LIGHT := Color(1.0, 0.55, 0.2) const BARS_PER_CELL := 4 const SHADER := """ shader_type spatial; render_mode unshaded, blend_add, cull_disabled, depth_draw_never, shadows_disabled; uniform vec4 col : source_color = vec4(1.0, 0.18, 0.12, 1.0); uniform float fade = 1.0; void fragment() { // Barrotes verticales que suben, más intensos abajo y en los bordes de la columna float bars = smoothstep(0.75, 1.0, abs(sin(UV.x * 18.0))); float flow = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(UV.y * 22.0 - TIME * 5.0 + UV.x * 6.0); float rim = pow(1.0 - abs(dot(NORMAL, VIEW)), 2.0); float bottom = 1.0 - UV.y * 0.6; float a = (0.18 + 0.55 * bars * flow + 0.5 * rim) * bottom * fade; ALBEDO = col.rgb * (1.5 + bars * 2.0); ALPHA = clamp(a, 0.0, 1.0); } """ static var _shader: Shader var _mat: ShaderMaterial var _body: StaticBody3D var _open := false var _bars := false ## reja de las cloacas en vez de energía ## Crea (cerrada) una barrera sobre las celdas `cells` (posiciones de mundo). static func spawn(parent: Node, cells: Array) -> DungeonDoor: var d := DungeonDoor.new() parent.add_child(d) d._build(cells) return d func _build(cells: Array) -> void: var bars: bool = WorldDefs.get_def(GameData.world).get("door", "runes") == "bars" _bars = bars if _shader == null: _shader = Shader.new() _shader.code = SHADER _mat = ShaderMaterial.new() _mat.shader = _shader _body = StaticBody3D.new() _body.collision_layer = 1 _body.collision_mask = 0

Serves both the refresh tool and the wait_for_idle tool ## (wait_for_idle is the idle-wait alone; refresh rescans then waits then reloads). ## ## Stateless — each handler takes (parameters) and returns the response Dictionary. ## The error-buffer flush (clear_level) is reached via the Modules alias; the rescan ## itself goes straight to EditorInterface.get_resource_filesystem() / ## get_script_editor(). The per-tile-edit policy (which keys are legal per verb, the ## _EDIT_* tables + _foreign_key_error gate) and its mechanism (how each key ## mutates TileData, the _apply_* flows + geometry builders) are inseparable, so ## they live together here. Persistence, the layer-node hint, and the full-tile ## polygon come from the shared tileset_io.gd leaf (_IO); consumed by ## tileset_commands.gd via a `preload` alias. const _IO := preload("res://addons/godot_mcp_toolkit/commands/tileset/tileset_io.gd") # -- Per-verb key enforcement ------------------------------------------------- # # Each tileset.edit_* tool owns exactly one tile-data concern. The five tools all # share cmd_edit, so without enforcement a key meant for one verb (e.g. # terrain_set) applied silently under another (e.g. edit_physics). These tables # make the verb authoritative: a verb accepts only its own per-tile keys plus the # universal coordinate selectors, and any foreign key is rejected with a hint that # names the tool that DOES own it (reverse lookup via _EDIT_KEY_OWNER). ## Coordinate selectors every verb needs to address a tile. const _EDIT_COORD_KEYS := ["atlas_x", "atlas_y"] ## Per-tile keys each verb is allowed to read/apply. nodes.summary: @tool extends RefCounted ## Canonical project-root identity for the multi-instance registry. ## ## The normalized path is the `_key` the TypeScript bridge reads from ## projects.json; the 12-char hash names the per-instance entry file ## (entries/<hash>.json) AND — via ProjectPaths — the per-instance user:// dir. ## ONE canonicalization recipe, two consumers: any change to the recipe shifts ## both the bridge-read key and the on-disk filenames, so it is frozen contract. ## ## All methods are static — identity by value, no instance state, no lifecycle. ## Canonicalize a project-root path: backslash → slash, strip trailing slash, ## and lowercase on case-insensitive filesystems. A lock ## is treated as stale — and overwritten — when its writer PID is dead or its ## timestamp is older than the staleness window, so a crashed holder never wedges ## the lock permanently. As a last resort the lock is force-written so the caller ## can always make progress. ## ## Both methods are static — no instance state; the lock path is passed in. ## Export-clean (FileAccess/OS/Time/DirAccess only) so runtime-reachable callers ## may preload it without tainting their static graph. const _LOCK_STALE_SEC := 10 const _LOCK_BASE_RETRY_MS := 50 const _LOCK_MAX_RETRY_MS := 1000 const _LOCK_RETRIES := 10 ## Returns true if the lock was acquired. nodes.summary: @tool extends RefCounted ## Presents an editor popup dialog: opens it centered and raises it to the front. ## ## A non-exclusive editor dialog sinks behind the main viewport the moment the ## viewport is clicked; re-triggering its opener button would then re-render the ## already-open-but-hidden window and feel unresponsive. nodes.summary: @tool extends RefCounted ## Append-only MCP audit log at ## user://addons/godot_mcp_toolkit/project_instance_<hash>/mcp_audit.log. ## ## Each tool dispatch writes one line: ## <ISO8601Z>\t<method>\t<params_sha256_hex[:12]> ## ## Opened and flushed per write for crash safety. const ProjectPaths := preload("res://addons/godot_mcp_toolkit/paths/project_paths.gd") static func get_log_path() -> String: return ProjectPaths.instance_dir() + "mcp_audit.log" static func log_call(method: String, parameters: Dictionary) -> void: if not ProjectSettings.get_setting("mcp_toolkit/audit/enabled", true): return var log_path := get_log_path() var timestamp := Time.get_datetime_string_from_system(true) + "Z" var params_hash := JSON.stringify(parameters).sha256_text().substr(0, 12) var line := "%s\t%s\t%s\n" % [timestamp, method, params_hash] var file: FileAccess = null if FileAccess.file_exists(log_path): file = FileAccess.open(log_path, FileAccess.READ_WRITE) if file != null: file.seek_end() else: ProjectPaths.ensure_dirs() file = FileAccess.open(log_path, FileAccess.WRITE) if file == null: push_warning("[Audit] could not open %s (err %d)" % [ log_path, FileAccess.get_open_error()]) return file.store_string(line) file.flush() var size := file.get_length() file.close() var max_kb: int = ProjectSettings.get_setting("mcp_toolkit/audit/max_size_kb", 1024) if max_kb > 0 and size > max_kb * 1024: _truncate_log(max_kb * 1024) static func _truncate_log(max_bytes: int) -> void: var log_path := get_log_path() var file := FileAccess.open(log_path, FileAccess.READ) if file == null: return var size := file.get_length() if size <= max_bytes: file.close() return # Keep the most recent ~50% of the limit so we don't truncate on every write. var keep := max_bytes / 2 file.seek(size - keep) file.get_line() # discard partial first line var remaining := file.get_as_text() file.close() var out := FileAccess.open(log_path, FileAccess.WRITE)

nodes.summary: class_name HealthComponent extends Node signal health_changed(hp, max_hp) signal entity_died # Used to modify damage before it is applied. Listeners can modify data["amount"]. signal damage_taking(data: Dictionary) @export var max_hp: float = 100.0 var hp: float var time_since_damage: float = 0.0 var invincibility_time: float = 0.0 var hp_regen: float = 0.0 ## vida por segundo (la fija PlayerStatBlock) var _regen_accum: float = 0.0 func _ready() -> void: hp = max_hp func _process(delta: float) -> void: if invincibility_time > 0: invincibility_time -= delta time_since_damage += delta _handle_hp_regen(delta) func is_invincible() -> bool: return invincibility_time > 0.0 func set_invincibility(duration: float) -> void: invincibility_time = maxf(invincibility_time, duration) func _handle_hp_regen(delta: float) -> void: if hp_regen <= 0.0 or hp <= 0.0 or hp >= max_hp: _regen_accum = 0.0 return _regen_accum += hp_regen * delta if _regen_accum >= 0.1: # curar a golpes de 0.1 para no emitir señales cada frame var amount := _regen_accum _regen_accum = 0.0 hp = min(max_hp, hp + amount) _emit_stats() func take_damage(amount: float) -> void: if invincibility_time > 0: return invincibility_time = 1.0 # 1.0 seconds of i-frames time_since_damage = 0.0 var data = {"amount": amount} damage_taking.emit(data) var final_amount: float = data["amount"] _default_damage(final_amount) _emit_stats() if hp <= 0: entity_died.emit() func _default_damage(amount: float) -> void: hp = max(0.0, hp - amount) func heal(amount: float) -> void: hp = min(max_hp, hp + amount) _emit_stats() func _emit_stats() -> void: health_changed.emit(hp, max_hp)

nodes.summary: class_name StatsComponent extends Node signal stats_changed(hp, max_hp) signal entity_died signal experience_gained(amount, current_xp, required_xp) signal leveled_up(new_level) @export var max_hp: float = 100.0 var hp: float var level: int = 1 var experience: float = 0.0 var experience_required: float = 10.0 var time_since_damage: float = 0.0 var invincibility_time: float = 0.0 var _parent: Node func _ready() -> void: hp = max_hp _parent = get_parent() func _process(delta: float) -> void: if invincibility_time > 0: invincibility_time -= delta time_since_damage += delta func take_damage(amount: float) -> void: if invincibility_time > 0: return invincibility_time = 1.0 # 1.0 seconds of i-frames time_since_damage = 0.0 var hp_damage := amount if _parent and "passive" in _parent and _parent.passive != null: if _parent.passive.has_method("on_take_damage"): hp_damage = _parent.passive.on_take_damage(_parent, amount) hp = max(0.0, hp - hp_damage) else: _default_damage(amount) else: _default_damage(amount) _emit_stats() if hp <= 0: emit_signal("entity_died") func _default_damage(amount: float) -> void: hp = max(0, hp - amount) func heal(amount: float) -> void: hp = min(max_hp, hp + amount) _emit_stats() func _emit_stats() -> void: emit_signal("stats_changed", hp, max_hp) func gain_experience(amount: float) -> void: experience += amount emit_signal("experience_gained", amount, experience, experience_required) while experience >= experience_required: experience -= experience_required level += 1 experience_required *= 1.5 # Incremental difficulty, this can be customized emit_signal("leveled_up", level) emit_signal("experience_gained", 0, experience, experience_required)

nodes.summary: class_name EnemyManager extends Node ## Gestiona a todos los enemigos normales (EnemyData): los crea/recicla por tipo (pool) y ejecuta la IA de ## todos en un único bucle de física. Vive como hijo del WaveManager. static var instance: EnemyManager = null static var _free: Dictionary = {} # tipo (int) -> Array[EnemyData] ## Nº de tick de física del bucle de enemigos: es el reloj con el que el shader de impostores interpola. static var tick: int = 0 var _active: Array = [] # EnemyData vivos var _player: Node3D = null func _ready() -> void: instance = self process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_PAUSABLE physics_interpolation_mode = Node.PHYSICS_INTERPOLATION_MODE_OFF func _exit_tree() -> void: if instance == self: instance = null _free.clear() _active.clear() ## Un solo bucle para todos los enemigos de datos. func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void: tick += 1 var vis := EnemyVisuals.instance var tick_f := float(tick) var i := 0 while i < _active.size(): var e: EnemyData = _active[i] e.tick_age += 1 if e.tick_age >= e.tick_span: # Actualiza con el tiempo acumulado de los ticks que se saltó var dt := delta * float(e.tick_age) e.tick_age = 0 e.update(dt) if vis != null: vis.write(e, tick_f) # Si e (u otro anterior) se recicló durante su update, la lista se desplazó: no se avanza if i < _active.size() and _active[i] == e: i += 1 # ───────────────────────────── Acceso estático ───────────────────────────── static func player_node() -> Node3D: if instance == null: return null if instance._player == null or not is_instance_valid(instance._player): instance._player = instance.get_tree().get_first_node_in_group("player") return instance._player static func scene_root() -> Node: return instance.get_tree().current_scene if instance != null and instance.is_inside_tree() else null static func floor_y(x: float, z: float) -> float: var root := scene_root() if root != null and root.has_method("get_floor_y")

nodes.summary: @tool class_name MCPToolkitUndoRedoAction extends RefCounted ## Fluent UndoRedo builder for MCP toolkit tools and extensions. ## ## Wraps [code]EditorUndoRedoManager[/code] with an automatic headless-safe no-op, ## an [code]"MCP: "[/code] action-name prefix, and a chainable builder API. Start ## with [method begin], record the do-side and undo-side with the ## [method do_property] / [method undo_property] (and [method do_method] / ## [method undo_method], [method do_reference] / [method undo_reference]) pairs, ## then close with [method commit_recorded] or [method commit]. Every builder ## method is a no-op when [method is_active] is [code]false[/code] (headless), so ## the same code runs safely with no editor.[br] ## [br] ## Recommended pattern — apply the mutation first, then record it for undo with ## [method commit_recorded]: ## [codeblock] ## node.set(&"position", new_pos) ## MCPToolkitUndoRedoAction.begin("set position", node) \ ## .do_property(node, &"position", new_pos) \ ## .undo_property(node, &"position", old_pos) \ ## .commit_recorded() ## [/codeblock] ## C# extensions cannot call this GDScript static — use ## [method MCPToolkitCommandRegistry.create_undo_action] instead of [method begin]. const Modules := preload("res://addons/godot_mcp_toolkit/core/modules.gd") ## EditorUndoRedoManager — used for all operations (create, add, commit). ## Routing to the correct internal history is handled by the manager itself. var _mgr = null # untyped for headless compat var _active: bool = false var _committed: bool = false ## Creates an undo action and returns the builder to chain from. [param description] ## is the human-readable action name (auto-prefixed with [code]"MCP: "[/code]); ## [param context_object] is the optional scene-owning node, which tells Godot which ## scene's history the action belongs to (important for multi-tab editing). Returns ## a builder bound to [code]EditorUndoRedoManager[/code], or a no-op builder in a ## headless context

nodes.summary: class_name FootIKModifier extends SkeletonModifier3D ## Animación procedural de pies: se aplica DESPUÉS de la animación (AnimationTree) ## y corrige las piernas con IK de dos huesos (muslo → pierna → pie): ## - Los pies nunca atraviesan el suelo (sentadillas y clavados exagerados). ## - En terreno irregular cada pie sigue la altura real del suelo bajo él y la ## cadera baja lo necesario para que el pie más bajo llegue. ## Solo actúa con el jugador en el suelo; en el aire se desvanece (influence). const LEGS := [ ["mixamorig_LeftUpLeg", "mixamorig_LeftLeg", "mixamorig_LeftFoot"], ["mixamorig_RightUpLeg", "mixamorig_RightLeg", "mixamorig_RightFoot"], ] const HIPS := "mixamorig_Hips" const BLEND_SPEED := 10.0 ## velocidad de entrada/salida del IK (1/s) const PELVIS_SPEED := 12.0 ## suavizado del ajuste de cadera (1/s) const MAX_PELVIS_DROP := 0.45 ## m var player: CharacterBody3D var _bones: Array = [] # [[upleg, leg, foot], ...] índices var _hips: int = -1 var _ankle_h: float = -1.0 # altura del tobillo sobre el suelo en reposo (m), medida en juego var _pelvis: float = 0.0 # desplazamiento actual de cadera (m, mundo) var _weight: float = 0.0 ## Altura (mundo) del pie más bajo tras aplicar el IK en el último frame (depuración/pruebas). var last_lowest_foot: float = 0.0 func setup(p_player: CharacterBody3D) -> bool: player = p_player var skel := get_skeleton() if skel == null: return false _hips = skel.find_bone(HIPS) _bones.clear() for leg in LEGS: var ids := [skel.find_bone(leg[0]), skel.find_bone(leg[1]), skel.find_bone(leg[2])] if ids.has(-1): return false _bones.append(ids) return _hips >= 0 func _floor_y(x: float, z: float) -> float: var map := get_tree().get_first_node_in_group("procedural_map") if map and map.has_method("get_height_at"): return map.get_height_at(x, z) return player.global_position.y func _process_modification_with_delta(delta: float) -> void: var skel := get_skeleton() if skel

nodes.summary: class_name HandIKModifier extends SkeletonModifier3D ## IK de las dos manos sobre un arma sujeta (solo mazmorra): lleva cada muñeca a su objetivo ## (RHTarget / LHTarget del ancla del arma) con IK analítico de dos huesos y un polo explícito para ## el codo, conservando la orientación animada de la mano. La mezcla la da `influence` ## (PlayerAnimationController la sube al equipar el arma). const ARMS := [["mixamorig_RightArm", "mixamorig_RightForeArm", "mixamorig_RightHand"], ["mixamorig_LeftArm", "mixamorig_LeftForeArm", "mixamorig_LeftHand"]] var targets: Array[Node3D] = [null, null] var poles: Array[Node3D] = [null, null] ## Pivote del arma: se coloca en el hombro derecho animado antes de resolver (el ancla cuelga de él) var pivot: Node3D var _ids := [] func setup(skel: Skeleton3D, rh: Node3D, lh: Node3D, pole_r: Node3D, pole_l: Node3D) -> bool: _ids.clear() for arm in ARMS: var ids := [] for b in arm: var i := skel.find_bone(b) if i < 0: return false ids.append(i) _ids.append(ids) targets = [rh, lh] poles = [pole_r, pole_l] return true func _process_modification_with_delta(_delta: float) -> void: var skel := get_skeleton() if skel == null or _ids.size() != 2: return if is_instance_valid(pivot): pivot.position = skel.get_bone_global_pose(_ids[0][0]).origin if influence <= 0.0: return var to_skel := skel.global_transform.affine_inverse() for i in 2: if not is_instance_valid(targets[i]) or not is_instance_valid(poles[i]): continue _solve(skel, _ids[i], to_skel * targets[i].global_position, to_skel * poles[i].global_position) ## Dos huesos (brazo, antebrazo) hacia `target`, con el codo en el plano que marca `pole`. func _solve(skel: Skeleton3D, ids: Array, target: Vector3, pole: Vector3) -> void: var pa := skel.get_bone_global_pose(ids[0]) var pb := skel.get_bone_global_pose(ids[1]) var pc := skel.get_bone_global_pose(ids[2]) var a := pa.origin var b := pb.origin var c := pc.origin var len_a := a.distance_to(b)

nodes.summary: class_name EnemyQuery extends RefCounted ## Detección de golpes contra enemigos SIN física: sustituye a get_overlapping_bodies(), body_entered y ## a los rayos físicos con máscara de enemigos. Trabaja con las posiciones del EnemyRegistry (y su ## rejilla espacial) y trata a cada enemigo como una cápsula vertical (hit_radius × hit_height). ## ## Cualquier cosa del registro debe exponer global_position y, opcionalmente, hit_radius / hit_height. const DEFAULT_RADIUS := 0.45 const DEFAULT_HEIGHT := 1.6 static func radius_of(e: Object) -> float: var r = e.get("hit_radius") return float(r) if r != null else DEFAULT_RADIUS static func height_of(e: Object) -> float: var h = e.get("hit_height") return float(h) if h != null else DEFAULT_HEIGHT # ───────────────────────────── Áreas (sustituye get_overlapping_bodies) ───────────────────────────── ## Enemigos que solapan con alguna CollisionShape3D del área (caja, esfera, cápsula o cilindro). static func overlapping(area: Area3D) -> Array: var out: Array = [] if not is_instance_valid(area) or not area.is_inside_tree(): return out for child in area.get_children(): if not (child is CollisionShape3D): continue var cs := child as CollisionShape3D if cs.disabled or cs.shape == null: continue var xf := cs.global_transform var reach := _shape_reach(cs.shape, xf) + 2.5 # + alto/radio de un enemigo for e in EnemyRegistry.query_radius(xf.origin, reach): if not out.has(e) and _enemy_touches_shape(e, cs.shape, xf): out.append(e) return out ## true si algún enemigo solapa con el área (para proyectiles que estallan al tocar). static func any_overlapping(area: Area3D) -> bool: return not overlapping(area).is_empty() static func _shape_reach(shape: Shape3D, xf: Transform3D) -> float: var s := xf.basis.get_scale() var smax := maxf(s.x, maxf(s.y, s.z)) if shape is SphereShape3D: return (shape as SphereShape3D).radius * smax if shape is BoxShape3D: return (shape as BoxShape3D).size.length() * 0

nodes.label: enemy_registry.gd
nodes.summary: class_name EnemyRegistry extends RefCounted ## Lista única de enemigos vivos. Sustituye a get_nodes_in_group("enemies") en los ## bucles por frame (armas, orbes, proyectiles): no crea un Array nuevo en cada llamada. ## Los enemigos se registran en _ready() y se dan de baja al salir del árbol (o al morir). ## all() devuelve la lista interna: se puede recorrer, pero NO modificar. static var _enemies: Array = [] ## Posición de cada objeto dentro de _enemies (objeto -> índice): alta/baja en O(1) con swap-remove. static var _index: Dictionary = {} ## Rejilla espacial (celdas de CELL m en XZ) para consultar "enemigos cerca de X" sin recorrerlos todos. ## Se reconstruye como mucho una vez por frame de física, la primera vez que alguien consulta. ## Los Arrays de las celdas se reutilizan entre reconstrucciones (no se reserva memoria cada frame). const CELL := 6.0 static var _grid: Dictionary = {} static var _grid_frame: int = -1 static var _query_buf: Array = [] static func _cell_of(x: float, z: float) -> Vector2i: return Vector2i(int(floor(x / CELL)), int(floor(z / CELL))) static func _rebuild_grid() -> void: for cell in _grid.values(): (cell as Array).clear() for e in _enemies: var c := _cell_of(e.global_position.x, e.global_position.z) if _grid.has(c): (_grid[c] as Array).append(e) else: _grid[c] = [e] ## Enemigos a distancia <= radius de `pos` (distancia 3D). Devuelve un Array nuevo, se puede modificar. static func query_radius(pos: Vector3, radius: float) -> Array: var out: Array = [] query_radius_into(pos, radius, out) return out ## Igual que query_radius pero rellena `out` (que se vacía antes): permite reutilizar el Array en bucles calientes. static func query_radius_into(pos: Vector3, radius: float, out: Array) -> void: out.clear() var frame := Engine.get_physics_frames() if frame != _grid_frame: _grid_frame = frame _rebuild_grid() var r2 := radius * radius var c0 := _cell_of(pos.x - radius, pos.z - radius) var c1 := _cell_of(pos

nodes.label: main.gd
nodes.summary: extends Node3D ## Main — punto de entrada de la escena de juego. ## Ahora delega toda la orquestación de subsistemas al GameStartFacade. @onready var hud = $HUD @onready var player = $Player var facade: GameStartFacade func _ready() -> void: # --- APLICACIÓN DEL PATRÓN FACADE --- # En lugar de crear y conectar 4+ managers manualmente, # delegamos todo a la fachada. facade = GameStartFacade.new() facade.name = "GameStartFacade" add_child(facade) facade.initialize(self, hud, player) # Main solo escucha las señales que le interesan a través de la fachada facade.restart_pressed.connect(restart) facade.enemy_died.connect(_on_enemy_died) facade.boss_died.connect(_on_boss_died) if player.has_signal("player_died"): player.connect("player_died", _on_player_died) var bench := EnemyBenchmark.from_env() if bench != null: add_child(bench) ## Reintentar: recarga la escena entera. Reiniciar a mano el jugador dejaba restos de la partida anterior ## (estado de muerte, jefe y enemigos vivos, armas, nivel de mazmorra, efectos, proyectiles...), así que ## se parte siempre de una escena limpia; lo único que sobrevive es lo guardado (oro, personaje elegido). func restart() -> void: get_tree().paused = false Engine.time_scale = 1.0 EnemyRegistry.clear() GameState.get_instance().reset_session() get_tree().reload_current_scene.call_deferred() func _process(delta: float) -> void: if not get_tree().paused: GameState.get_instance().add_time(delta) facade.update_elapsed_time(GameState.get_instance().elapsed_time) func get_floor_y(x: float, z: float) -> float: return facade.get_floor_y(x, z) func _input(event: InputEvent) -> void: if event is InputEventKey and event.pressed and not event.echo: if event.keycode == KEY_F9: var existing := get_node_or_null("EnemyBenchmark") if existing != null: existing.queue_free() else: var b := EnemyBenchmark.new() b.name = "EnemyBenchmark" add_child(b) elif event.keycode == KEY_Y: facade.s

nodes.label: remote_player.gd
nodes.summary: class_name RemotePlayer extends CharacterBody3D ## Representación de otro jugador de la red. No se mueve por física: su dueño manda el estado (posición, ## giro, velocidad, arma) y aquí se interpola. Se ve con el MISMO controlador de animación y las mismas ## armas en la mano que el jugador local (PlayerAnimationController + PlayerWeaponVisuals): su dueño avisa de ## cada acción (golpes, rodar, disparos) y aquí se reproducen igual. Para la IA enemiga y los proyectiles se ## comporta como un jugador: está en el grupo "net_players" y tiene take_damage(), que reenvía el golpe a su ## dueño (que es quien lleva su vida real). signal weapon_attacked(weapon_type: int) ## el controlador de animación espera esta señal del jugador var peer_id := 0 var char_index := 0 var net_char_id := "" ## lo lee PlayerAnimationController (_char_id) var net_on_floor := true ## ídem (no se puede sobrescribir is_on_floor) var weapon := -1 var hp := 1.0 var max_hp := 1.0 var move_speed := 7.0 var mesh: Node3D ## como Player.mesh: el modelo cuelga de aquí var weapon_visuals: Node var weapon_models: Dictionary = {} var animation_controller: PlayerAnimationController var _target_pos := Vector3.ZERO var _target_yaw := 0.0 var _label: Label3D var _got_state := false func _ready() -> void: add_to_group("net_players") collision_layer = 2 collision_mask = 0 var col := CollisionShape3D.new() var cap := CapsuleShape3D.new() cap.radius = 0.35 cap.height = 1.7 col.shape = cap col.position.y = 0.9 add_child(col) mesh = Node3D.new() mesh.name = "KnightMesh" add_child(mesh) var ch: Dictionary = GameData.CHARACTERS[clampi(char_index, 0, GameData.CHARACTERS.size() - 1)] net_char_id = str(ch["id"]) move_speed = float(ch.get("stats", {}).get("move_speed", 7.0)) * GameData.DUNGEON_MOVE_SPEED_MULT # Mismo esqueleto, animaciones y armas en la mano que el jugador local weapon_visuals = load("res://scripts/entities/player_weapon_visuals.gd"
